'''''Cleome houtteana''''', commonly known as '''spider flower''', '''spider plant''',<ref name=huxley/> '''pink queen''',<ref name=grin/> or '''grandfather's whiskers''',<ref>{{Cite web| title=Tarenaya houtteana (Schltdl.) Soares Neto & Roalson | publisher=NParks Singapore | url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/3/3/3313}}</ref>  is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Cleome]]'' of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Cleomaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to southern South America in Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, and southeast Brazil.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN}}</ref> It has also been introduced to South Asia, including the Haor area of Bangladesh and India.
<ref>{{Cite web| title=ফুলের নাম পিউম (The name of the flower is peum)| language=bn| publisher=Prothomalo | date=2018-04-19| url=http://www.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/article/1472506/ফুলের-নাম-পিউম}}</ref>

It is an [[annual plant|annual]] growing to a height of {{convert|150|cm|-1|abbr=on}}, with spirally arranged leaves. It has a height of 90 cm (35 in) to 180 cm (71 in). The [[leaf|leaves]] are [[Glossary of leaf morphology|palmately]] compound, with five or seven leaflets, the leaflets up to {{convert|12|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|4|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad and the leaf petiole up to {{convert|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} long. Its maximum crown width ranges from 30 cm (12 in) to 60 cm (24 in). The [[flower]]s are purple, pink, or white, with four petals and six long stamens. The [[fruit]] is a [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]] up to 15 cm long and {{convert|3|mm|1|abbr=on}} broad, containing several seeds. Flowering lasts from late spring to early fall.<ref name=huxley>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening'' 1: 652. Macmillan {{ISBN|1-56159-001-0}}.</ref>

The scented blooms are sometimes compared to [[Pelargonium citrosum|citronella]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=White |first1=Jay |title=Spider Flower (Cleome hasslerana) |url=http://masterofhort.com/2011/07/spider-flower-cleome-hasslerana/ |website=masterofhort.com |accessdate=19 March 2020}}</ref>

''Cleome houtteana'' is commonly cultivated in [[Temperate climate|temperate]] regions as a [[Hardiness (plants)|half-hardy]] [[annual plant|annual]]. Numerous [[cultivar]]s have been selected for flower color and other attributes. The "Queen" series includes the cultivars 'Violet Queen', 'Rose Queen', and 'White Queen'. The cultivar 'Helen Campbell' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/106100/i-Cleome-hassleriana-i-Helen-Campbell/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Cleome hassleriana''
| accessdate = 30 January 2018}}</ref> (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 22 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 24 January 2018}}</ref> 

== Misidentification ==
[[File:Cleome houtteana at Felda Sungai Sayong in Kota Tinggi, Johor 20250401 130156.jpg|thumb|left|The leaves of this species resemble cannibis]]
The plant is sometimes mistakenly identified as [[cannabis]] due to its leaves and general growth shape. It also shares a similar odor, a foetid or skunky smell produced by the glandular hairs.<ref>https://hort.extension.wisc.edu/articles/spider-flower-cleome-hassleriana</ref>

Plants in cultivation have also at times been misidentified as ''Cleome arborea'', ''C. pungens'' or ''C. spinosa''.<ref name=grin/>
